clue.text: Some will have gathered to justify this thanksgiving

definitions.text: Some will have gathered to justify this thanksgiving

parts.words: Some will have gathered to justify this thanksgiving
parts.note: the crops must first be brought in before a church service of gratitude for them can be held

explanation.surface: A congregation has assembled to give a reason for its thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathered' reads as people assembling, but it is crops being brought in from the fields; the autumn church thanksgiving celebrates that.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumn church celebration gives thanks for crops successfully reaped and brought in.

clue.text: Distance we must go in trapping seabird in US port

indicators.note: the word we has to be placed within the distance word

parts.note: a mile is a distance

indicators.note: the we letters hold the seabird between them

parts.note: taken as written
the auk is a diving seabird

explanation.surface: Someone must travel some distance in a US port while catching a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must go in' and 'trapping' are two nested containers: the seabird sits inside 'we', and that pair sits inside the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wisconsin city lies on Lake Michigan and is a Great Lakes shipping harbour.

clue.text: Way marsupial first creates sleeping-place

indicators.note: says the marsupial comes before the way in the answer

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A kangaroo leading the way makes itself a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's perch for the night is a place to sleep.

clue.text: Antiseptic used by filthy molecatchers

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Dirty mole-catchers rely on a germ-killing preparation.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound from thyme oil, it is used to kill germs in mouthwashes and dressings.

clue.text: Chap in work is initially true Panglossian type

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
Tim is a man's name, a chap

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A man at work is at first a truly cheerful sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Pangloss in Voltaire's Candide insists all is for the best in the best of all possible worlds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes everything will turn out well is a relentlessly hopeful person, like Pangloss.

clue.text: Observe swimmer in brightly coloured coat

indicators.note: the fish goes inside the colour word

parts.note: red is a bright colour
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Watch a fish with a vivid coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at or observe it.

clue.text: Right to wear women's underwear where food is kept?

indicators.note: the underwear is put on by, so surrounds, the R

parts.note: panties are women's knickers

explanation.surface: Someone is entitled to don ladies' knickers in the larder.
explanation.definitionFit: Small storerooms off a kitchen are used for keeping provisions.

clue.text: Possible exit men used after gin party?

indicators.note: the men are placed after the gin and party pieces

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap
a do is a party
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers turn up after a drinks party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged door in a floor or ceiling can serve as a way out.

clue.text: Overcoming resistance, arrived at cave

indicators.note: the arrival phrase sits over and around the resistance letter

parts.note: got to means arrived at
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Beating opposition, someone reached a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cavern.

clue.text: Furniture-maker cross about note containing directions

indicators.note: the cross word goes around the rest

parts.note: a rood is a cross, especially in a church

indicators.note: the note holds the directions inside

parts.note: so (or soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
E and W are east and west, compass directions

explanation.surface: An angry joiner is irritated about a piece of music with instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furniture-maker' suggests a carpenter, but it is the timber the furniture is made from; 'cross' reads as angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark tropical hardwood prized for making fine cabinets and tables.

clue.text: What we may see, having this drink?

definitions.meaning: seeing twin images, as a drinker's blurred vision does

explanation.surface: Asking what someone sees after a particular drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Blurred drunken vision shows twin images, and a bar measure of spirits twice the standard size shares the name.

clue.text: Frivolous airhead originally visiting at Newcastle, perhaps?

indicators.note: the letter goes into, visits, the place phrase

parts.note: in can mean at, as in at home
Newcastle is in the north-east, NE

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of airhead

explanation.surface: A scatterbrain is first off visiting Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle upon Tyne is the main city of England's north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and lacking sense or seriousness; senseless and trivial.

clue.text: Close associate Briony fed haphazardly

indicators.note: done haphazardly, the letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Briony gave a partner something to eat carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A male partner in a romantic relationship is a close companion.

clue.text: Girth problem quietly studied after centuries in the past

indicators.note: the quiet and studied pieces follow the past centuries

parts.note: the Middle Ages are the medieval centuries
p (piano) means quietly in music
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A weight problem was examined softly after many years back.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickening of the waist that comes with reaching one's forties or fifties.

clue.text: Possible pet manuscript spiteful person's hidden

indicators.note: the hater has the manuscript tucked away inside

parts.note: a hater is a spiteful person; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A pet document has been concealed by someone malicious.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent commonly kept in a cage as a companion animal.

clue.text: Party leader leaves match for track event

indicators.note: that letter departs from the match word

parts.note: a replay is a match played again

indicators.note: the leader of party is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political chief walks out of a match to watch athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: A team race on the athletics track in which runners hand over a baton.

clue.text: Besotted woman married the Times boss?

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name
our ed: our editor, as this newspaper's setter would say

explanation.surface: A woman wed the newspaper's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared in The Times, so its editor is 'our ed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deeply in love or infatuated means being smitten with someone.

clue.text: Nick's interpretation?

definitions.meaning: to nick is to steal or pinch
one's personal view or reading of events

explanation.surface: Asking how a man called Nick reads something.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for stealing matches it, and so does a personal view or reading of a situation.

clue.text: Former politician in real trouble, for instance

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the politician goes inside the scrambled letters
real in trouble is disordered into a new arrangement

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An ex-MP in genuine difficulty, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former politician' looks like one person, an ex-MP, but the ex and the MP are separate pieces; 'trouble' rearranges REAL as ELAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A model or typical case is offered as an example, which 'for instance' introduces.

clue.text: Bones found in Saul's place, one required for you and me

indicators.note: one letter is needed in place of the pronoun

parts.note: Saul (St Paul) came from Tarsus
you and me together are us
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Skeleton parts discovered at the apostle's hometown.
explanation.walkthrough: In TARSUS, US is replaced by I.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle bones, plural of tarsus.

clue.text: I bow and scrape, though I could be the leader

definitions.text: I bow and scrape, though I could be the leader

parts.words: I bow and scrape, though I could be the leader
parts.note: the bowing and scraping are on strings, not servility, and the orchestra's leader is the principal of the firsts

explanation.surface: A fawning underling who might yet be in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British orchestra the leader is the principal first-desk string player.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra's leader is the first player of this bowed string instrument.

clue.text: No small task, for example, unravelling TS Eliot!

indicators.note: the poet's name is untangled and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Picking apart a poet's work is no easy job.
explanation.definitionFit: Understatement by denying the opposite, as 'no small task' means a big one.

clue.text: Plain animal left in imposing surroundings

indicators.note: the imposing word surrounds the others

parts.note: grand means imposing
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A simple beast was abandoned amid grand settings.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain is open flat country covered with grass.

clue.text: Something fishy, almost, over support for jet engine

indicators.note: in a down entry, the fish part sits above the support
the fish loses its final letter

parts.note: a turbot is a flatfish
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: Something suspicious nearly topped the jet's mounting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas turbine engine driving a propeller is a type of jet engine.

clue.text: State of officer with high honour born north of Iowa

indicators.note: in a down entry the earlier pieces stand above Iowa

parts.note: Col is short for colonel
the OM, Order of Merit, is a high British honour
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: The record of a decorated soldier born north of Iowa.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM (Order of Merit) is an exclusive British honour in the monarch's gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American country, a nation or state.

clue.text: Play is Miller's first, enshrining Republican ideology

indicators.note: the play word holds the next letter within it

parts.note: to toy is to play
taken as written

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A drama by Arthur Miller featuring a Republican creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservative political belief, the doctrine of the Tory party.

clue.text: Exaggerated fuss once upset composer being admitted

indicators.note: the composer is let inside the reversed word
in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: do was once a word for fuss or ado
Verdi wrote Aida and La Traviata

explanation.surface: An old fuss went wrong when an opera writer was let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' for a fuss is now dated, hence 'once'; 'upset' in a down clue reads the word bottom to top, giving OD.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it too far, overstating or overacting it.

clue.text: Potter's device located at first with excited cry

parts.note: whee is a cry of glee

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of located

explanation.surface: A pottery tool is found with a shout of delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Potters shape clay on a revolving disc called a wheel.

clue.text: Note from bishop disheartened old magistrate

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the magistrate loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: a reeve was a local magistrate in medieval England

explanation.surface: A message from a bishop dispirited an old official.
explanation.definitionFit: A long musical note, equal to two semibreves.

clue.text: Person forking out, we hear, for neat accommodation

indicators.note: says the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a buyer pays, forking out money

explanation.surface: Someone paying up is heard about tidy lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle, so neat accommodation is a cowshed.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, housing for cattle.
